status_reasoning: Reviewers express major concerns about the claimed resolution, stating 'a resolution that is significantly lower than 3.9 Angstroms will draw into question the validity of the model building.' They request gold-standard FSC and map/model FSC analyses, noting that 'many single particle procedures are susceptible to overfitting of noise, which gives rise to inflated resolution claims.' The expectation is that 'the revised manuscript will state a lower resolution,' indicating uncertainty about the reported 3.9 Å resolution.

Reviewers specifically question the validity of the de novo model of FrhB, stating that 'a resolution that is significantly lower than 3.9 Angstroms will draw into question the validity of the model building, especially the de novo model of FrhB.' They request that authors 'make a strong case of why the map is still of sufficient quality to build a reliable de novo model,' indicating uncertainty about whether the map quality supports the ab initio modeling claims for this novel subunit.

Reviewers explicitly accept the overall architecture findings, noting that 'The enzyme is shown to form a spherical protein shell (Td symmetry) that contains 12 copies of the heterotrimeric building block (correcting previous models for the assembly).' This indicates reviewer acceptance of the dodecameric structure and tetrahedral symmetry claims without expressing concerns about these specific findings.

Reviewers acknowledge that 'Two of the trimer subunits have counterparts on the class I hydrogenases,' implicitly accepting the homology-based modeling of FrhA and FrhG. No concerns are raised about the structural comparisons or modeling of these subunits using known homologs, suggesting reviewer acceptance of these claims.

Reviewers accept that 'one subunit, which is unique to the group 3 enzymes, is a novel iron-sulfur flavoprotein,' acknowledging the identification of FrhB as a novel iron-sulfur flavoprotein with FAD and F420-binding site. While they question the de novo modeling quality, they do not dispute the identification of this subunit's composition and novelty.

While reviewers do not explicitly critique the F420 binding site identification, their concerns about overall map quality and resolution ('the quality of the density maps and the true resolution') indirectly affect confidence in substrate localization claims. The request for objective validation of map quality suggests uncertainty about detailed features like substrate positioning that depend on resolution quality.

Reviewers request 'an objective, quantitative comparison (cross-correlation) between the map and the model' and note that the map/model FSC at 5.8 Å (C118) should be evaluated against gold-standard metrics. They express concern that current validation may not adequately demonstrate model quality, requesting additional analyses to 'back their presentation of a few local regions of the structure,' indicating uncertainty about the model's overall reliability.

Reviewers do not question the background knowledge and established facts about [NiFe]-hydrogenases, methanogenesis, F420 function, or prior structural studies. These claims represent established knowledge cited from literature and are implicitly accepted as the reviewers focus their concerns on the new experimental findings rather than the contextual background.
